lab_title: The Human Heart: Structure and the Path of Blood Flow
top_level_objectives: Identify the four chambers of the heart (right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, left ventricle) and the four valves (tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral/bicuspid, aortic).
Locate and name the major vessels entering and leaving the heart (superior and inferior vena cava, pulmonary arteries, pulmonary veins, aorta).
Trace the dual-loop (pulmonary and systemic) circulation of blood through the heart in the correct sequence.
Explain why the left ventricle has a thicker myocardium than the right ventricle and how the valves prevent backflow during the cardiac cycle.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the heart as a whole organ and establish anatomical orientation so students can navigate the model in later scenes.
key_visuals: A life-sized, slowly rotating 3D human heart positioned upright in the student's space
Anatomical orientation markers indicating anterior/posterior, superior/inferior, and left/right
A semi-transparent outline of the thoracic cavity showing the heart nestled between the lungs
student_actions: Walk around the heart model to view it from anterior and posterior sides
Tap the orientation markers to confirm understanding of directional terms
Pinch to rotate and resize the heart to a comfortable viewing scale

scenes.brief_purpose: Help students identify and distinguish the four chambers and understand the division between the right and left sides of the heart.
key_visuals: A coronal cut-away view exposing all four hollow chambers
Color-coded chambers: right atrium and right ventricle in blue, left atrium and left ventricle in red
The interventricular and interatrial septa highlighted as the dividing walls
student_actions: Tap each chamber to reveal its name and a short description
Drag chamber labels onto the correct chambers in a matching challenge
Note and respond to a prompt about which side handles deoxygenated versus oxygenated blood

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the valves, their positions between chambers and vessels, and their role in ensuring one-way blood flow.
key_visuals: Close-up views of the tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral, and aortic valves in their anatomical locations
An animated valve opening and closing to show one-way flow
A demonstration of backflow being blocked when a valve closes
student_actions: Tap each valve to learn its name and the two regions it connects
Toggle a valve animation to observe opening and closing
Answer a short prompt predicting what would happen if a valve failed to close

scenes.brief_purpose: Identify the great vessels that carry blood into and out of the heart and connect them to their respective chambers.
key_visuals: The heart with the superior and inferior vena cava, pulmonary arteries, pulmonary veins, and aorta extending from it
Vessels color-coded by oxygenation (blue for deoxygenated, red for oxygenated)
Arrows indicating whether each vessel carries blood toward or away from the heart
student_actions: Tap each vessel to reveal its name and the chamber it connects to
Sort vessels into 'entering the heart' and 'leaving the heart' categories
Identify which vessels carry oxygenated blood despite naming conventions (e.g., pulmonary veins)

scenes.brief_purpose: Synthesize chambers, valves, and vessels by following a unit of blood through the complete dual-loop circulation.
key_visuals: An animated stream of color-changing blood particles flowing through the heart in sequence
A highlighted pathway that lights up each structure as the blood reaches it
A split-view diagram showing the pulmonary loop and systemic loop side by side
student_actions: Step through the circulation pathway one structure at a time, tapping to advance
Watch blood change from blue to red as it passes through the lungs and back
Reconstruct the correct sequence of structures in an ordering exercise

scenes.scene_name: Why the Left Ventricle Is Thicker
scenes.brief_purpose: Connect structure to function by comparing the myocardial wall thickness of the two ventricles and explaining the pressure demands.
key_visuals: A cross-sectional comparison of the right and left ventricular walls with measurable thickness
A visual contrast of the short pulmonary loop versus the long systemic loop the blood must travel
A pressure gauge animation showing higher force generated by the left ventricle
student_actions: Measure or compare the wall thickness of each ventricle using an on-screen tool
Tap to view the distance blood travels in each circulatory loop
Answer a reflective prompt explaining the structural-functional relationship

scenes.brief_purpose: Consolidate learning and assess mastery of heart anatomy and blood flow through an interactive challenge.
key_visuals: An unlabeled heart model ready for student identification
A scoreboard or progress tracker showing completed identifications
A summary diagram of the full circulation pathway revealed upon completion
student_actions: Label all four chambers, four valves, and major vessels on the unlabeled model
Drag blood-flow arrows into the correct sequence to recreate the dual-loop pathway
Receive feedback and review any structures answered incorrectly
